memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very
edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Leave
them for the poor and for the foreigner residing among you. I am the
LORD your God'" - Lev 23:22 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Right in the middle of festival regulations, God inserts a command
about the poor. That placement is not accidental. Worship and
generosity were never meant to be separate departments.

The instruction is practical and dignified. Do not harvest the corners.
Do not go back for what was dropped. Leave it, and let those in need
come and gather it with their own hands. There was no queue, no
humiliation, no charity handout. Just margin deliberately built into
the harvest.

This is how Ruth met Boaz. She was a foreign widow gleaning at the
edges of a field, and she became the great-grandmother of David and an
ancestor of Jesus.

Dear reader, most of us reap to the very edges. We calculate carefully
so that nothing is wasted and every resource is optimised. Efficiency
is not wrong, but God asks for deliberate margin - room in our income,
our time and our energy for people in need.

James says religion that God accepts is this: to look after orphans
and widows in their distress (Jas 1:27). John asks how the love of God
can be in anyone who sees a brother in need and shows no pity (1 John
3:17).

Where are the edges of your field?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I built any margin into my life for others, or is everything
   optimised for me?
2. Who around me is quietly in need that I have not noticed?
3. What "edge" could I deliberately leave unharvested this month?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for reaping right to the edges of my life. Give me a
generous heart and open eyes to see those You want me to help. Amen.
